item.title: Escambia Children's Trust awards $3.6M in grants to 11 local health, family support projects
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Escambia Children's Trust has distributed $3,639,575 in Bright Beginnings grants to support early childhood development and family services across the county. Among the funded projects are a new doula program to support mothers during pregnancy and postpartum, funding for a full-time developmental pediatrician to serve young children with…
item.content:encoded:
The Escambia Children's Trust has distributed $3,639,575 in Bright Beginnings grants to support early childhood development and family services across the county.

Among the funded projects are a new doula program to support mothers during pregnancy and postpartum, funding for a full-time developmental pediatrician to serve young children with developmental concerns, and expanded services reaching into the Century and North Escambia County areas that have historically had fewer resources.

In total, 11 different projects were selected to receive funding through the competitive grant process. The awards reflect the trust's focus on giving young children in Escambia County a strong start through evidence-based programs and increased access to specialized care.

item.content:encoded: Pensacola and North Escambia are in for a stretch of pleasant fall weather over the next few days, with mostly sunny skies and warm afternoons expected through Friday. Highs should reach the upper 70s to low 80s, making it ideal weather for outdoor activities, while nights cool to the mid-50s to lower 60s. The pattern breaks down heading into the weekend, according to local forecasts, when rain chances increase. Residents should enjoy the dry weather window while it lasts and keep an eye on weekend forecasts for timing and intensity of potential precipitation.

item.content:encoded:
Two adults lost their home early Tuesday morning when a fire broke out in a two-story residence in Cantonment. Escambia County Fire Rescue responded around 4:53 a.m. to a house in the 2200 block of Riddle Road, off East Kingsfield Road, according to North Escambia. Firefighters found the blaze concentrated on the upper level of the home.

The displaced residents have been accounted for. No additional details on injuries, the fire's cause, or damage estimates were immediately available. The county fire department has not yet released further information about the incident.

item.title: AAA warns of Halloween road dangers Saturday night in Pensacola area
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: With Halloween falling on Saturday this year, the Auto Club Group is urging Pensacola-area drivers and families to exercise extra caution as neighborhoods fill with trick-or-treaters, weekend motorists, and riders on bikes and e-scooters after dark. According to AAA spokesman Mark Jenkins, the combination of increased foot traffic and weekend…
item.content:encoded:
With Halloween falling on Saturday this year, the Auto Club Group is urging Pensacola-area drivers and families to exercise extra caution as neighborhoods fill with trick-or-treaters, weekend motorists, and riders on bikes and e-scooters after dark.

According to AAA spokesman Mark Jenkins, the combination of increased foot traffic and weekend driving activity creates a particularly risky scenario. Safe Kids Worldwide reports that children are more than twice as likely to be struck and killed by a vehicle on Halloween than any other day of the year. Peak trick-or-treating hours—5:30 to 9:30 p.m.—coincide with darkness, compounding the hazard. Adding another layer of concern, federal data shows 201 people died in alcohol-related crashes on Halloween nights between 2020 and 2024.

AAA recommends drivers slow down in neighborhoods, eliminate distractions, and actively watch for pedestrians and cyclists. The organization also advises trick-or-treaters to wear reflective materials, carry flashlights, use crosswalks, and avoid stepping between parked cars. Parents should supervise children under 12 and ensure costumes don't obstruct vision or movement.

"Expect more people to be out after dark and slow down in neighborhoods," Jenkins said. "A child in a costume, or someone riding an e-bike or e-scooter, can appear in your path with very little warning."

The declaration makes federal Emergency Management Agency assistance available to a dozen Florida counties dealing with storm damage. While the report…
item.content:encoded:
The Trump Administration has approved a Major Disaster Declaration for Florida in the wake of Hurricane Isaias, which struck the state earlier this month, according to reporting from WKRG News 5.

The declaration makes federal Emergency Management Agency assistance available to a dozen Florida counties dealing with storm damage. While the report references comments from Pensacola Mayor D.C., the full details of which specific counties are included and the scope of available assistance were not fully detailed in the available reporting.

Major Disaster Declarations typically unlock various forms of federal aid, including grants for temporary housing, home repairs, and low-interest disaster loans for both individuals and businesses affected by the storm. The declaration comes as recovery efforts continue across the affected areas.

item.title: Democratic CFO candidate Taddeo joins Jolly-Graham tour stops in Jacksonville, Gainesville
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Democratic candidate for Florida Chief Financial Officer Annette Taddeo will campaign Wednesday alongside gubernatorial and lieutenant gubernatorial candidates David Jolly and Gwen Graham as part of their Believe in Better Tour, with stops planned in Jacksonville and Gainesville ahead of Election Day. The Jacksonville rally begins at 2 p.m.…
item.content:encoded:
Democratic candidate for Florida Chief Financial Officer Annette Taddeo will campaign Wednesday alongside gubernatorial and lieutenant gubernatorial candidates David Jolly and Gwen Graham as part of their Believe in Better Tour, with stops planned in Jacksonville and Gainesville ahead of Election Day.

The Jacksonville rally begins at 2 p.m. Wednesday at the International Longshoremen's Association hall on East 21st Street and will also feature Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Angie Nixon. That evening, Taddeo, Jolly, and Graham will hold a get-out-the-vote rally in Gainesville at the Woman's Club on University Avenue starting at 6 p.m.

Taddeo, a former state senator and small business owner, is running on a platform centered on affordability, accountability, and anti-corruption. According to her campaign, she aims to lower costs for Floridians, protect consumers, and combat government waste and corruption if elected to the statewide fiscal office. Media interested in covering either event can contact Ulysses del Pino at 786-527-0144.

item.title: Sen. Moody Secures $11M Federal Grant for Port of Fernandina Infrastructure
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Senator Ashley Moody has helped the Ocean Highway and Port Authority land an $11 million federal grant to address flooding and structural damage at the Port of Fernandina, according to a press release issued today. The Port Infrastructure Development Program funding will support flood mitigation and dock rehabilitation projects, including drainage…
item.content:encoded:
Senator Ashley Moody has helped the Ocean Highway and Port Authority land an $11 million federal grant to address flooding and structural damage at the Port of Fernandina, according to a press release issued today.

The Port Infrastructure Development Program funding will support flood mitigation and dock rehabilitation projects, including drainage system upgrades, water capture infrastructure, pumps for surge and rainfall events, crane rail repair, and structural reinforcement. The port has faced chronic flooding and deterioration that threatened its operational capacity and worker safety.

"Florida's ports are critical to our economy, supporting thousands of jobs and helping businesses move goods across the country and around the world," Moody said in a statement. The Port of Fernandina, located on the Amelia River, supports more than 4,600 jobs and generates nearly $1.3 billion in annual economic contributions to Northeast Florida, according to port authority data.

Moody had previously urged the U.S. Department of Transportation to approve the funding request in a June letter to Maritime Administration Administrator Captain Stephen Carmel. Congressman Aaron Bean (FL-04) also backed the grant, calling the port "a small but mighty, strategically vital, and irreplaceable asset" for the region's supply chain.

item.title: Fall Fun Across Santa Rosa County: Pumpkin Patches, Markets, and Car Show This Weekend
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County is packed with family-friendly activities this fall, with several events hitting their peak season through November and a couple of standout options this coming weekend. If you're looking for Halloween festivities, the 26th Annual Navarre Beach Autorama takes place Saturday, October 31st at Navarre High School, featuring over 150…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County is packed with family-friendly activities this fall, with several events hitting their peak season through November and a couple of standout options this coming weekend.

If you're looking for Halloween festivities, the 26th Annual Navarre Beach Autorama takes place Saturday, October 31st at Navarre High School, featuring over 150 classic and vintage cars, trucks, and bikes. The show runs from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., with music, food, and vendor booths. Check-in starts at 8, and judging begins at 11 a.m. That same morning, the Navarre Beach Sea Turtle Conservation Center is hosting a Halloween-themed Trash Bash from 8 to 10 a.m., encouraging volunteers in upcycled or marine-themed costumes to help clean up and protect sea turtles and other wildlife.

For ongoing fall activities, two major pumpkin patches are in full swing. Holland Farms Pumpkin Patch & Maze in Milton offers hayrides, train rides, a corn maze, zip lines, and an eight-acre corn maze, along with free boiled peanuts for every visitor. Sweet Season Farms, also in Milton, features its 18th annual corn maze plus u-pick pumpkins and sunflowers, with over 25 farm activities and a bakery serving caramel apples and kettle corn. Both are open daily through early November.

If you prefer shopping and dining, the Highway 87 Outdoor Market in Navarre sets up the first and third Saturday of each month with farm-to-table vendors and local crafts, while Sand Dollar Plaza in Navarre hosts community appreciation events every Saturday. For more details on any of these events, visit the Santa Rosa County tourism website or contact individual venues directly.

item.title: Eglin FCU honors Jamie Cervantes as Q3 Five-Star Performer
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Eglin Federal Credit Union has named Card Services Supervisor Jamie Cervantes its Five-Star Performer for the third quarter of 2026, recognizing her 17 years of service and leadership at the Fort Walton Beach-based credit union. Cervantes was nominated by multiple coworkers for her exceptional leadership, dedication to member service, and positive…
item.content:encoded:
Eglin Federal Credit Union has named Card Services Supervisor Jamie Cervantes its Five-Star Performer for the third quarter of 2026, recognizing her 17 years of service and leadership at the Fort Walton Beach-based credit union.

Cervantes was nominated by multiple coworkers for her exceptional leadership, dedication to member service, and positive attitude. The Five-Star Performer Award is a quarterly recognition program that honors employees who embody the credit union's core values: Respectful, Trustworthy, Dedicated, Proactive and Engaged.

Cervantes began her career at Eglin FCU in July 2009 as a part-time teller at the Fort Walton Beach branch. She has advanced through several positions in card services operations, including mail teller, EFT representative, and senior representative roles, before her promotion to Card Services Supervisor in July 2022. In that role, she oversees a team focused on delivering member support and internal service.

Card Services Manager Alicia Kennedy praised Cervantes in a statement, noting her willingness to step in and help colleagues and her ability to build trust quickly with members. "She is widely recognized throughout Eglin FCU as a trusted and knowledgeable resource," Kennedy said.

item.title: Jolly draws bigger crowd than Donalds at dueling Pensacola rallies

The competing events showcased the intensity of Florida's 2026 gubernatorial race, with both major party nominees…
item.content:encoded:
Democratic gubernatorial candidate David Jolly attracted a larger crowd than Republican opponent Byron Donalds when both candidates held campaign rallies in Pensacola on Monday, according to reporting from the Pensacola News Journal.

The competing events showcased the intensity of Florida's 2026 gubernatorial race, with both major party nominees making stops in the Panhandle to court voters in a key swing region. Pensacola and the surrounding Escambia County area have proven competitive in statewide elections, making Monday's dual rallies a significant show of campaign strength for both camps.

While crowd size is often used as a barometer of campaign momentum, political analysts caution that attendance figures don't necessarily predict electoral outcomes. Both campaigns appeared committed to making a strong impression in the Pensacola market ahead of the election.

item.title: Santa Rosa County Libraries announce November closures, programs
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County Libraries will close for Veterans Day on Wednesday, November 11, and for Thanksgiving from Thursday through Saturday, November 26–28. The library system is offering several programs throughout November. Preschool Storytime for ages 3–5 continues at locations across the county, including Gulf Breeze (Fridays at 11 a.m.), Jay…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County Libraries will close for Veterans Day on Wednesday, November 11, and for Thanksgiving from Thursday through Saturday, November 26–28.

The library system is offering several programs throughout November. Preschool Storytime for ages 3–5 continues at locations across the county, including Gulf Breeze (Fridays at 11 a.m.), Jay (Tuesdays at 11 a.m.), Milton (Wednesdays at 10:30 a.m.), Navarre (Tuesdays at 11 a.m.), and Pace (Thursdays at 11 a.m.). Toddler Time for ages 18–36 months requires registration and is available at all five locations on various days. Both programs run through December 4.

Special events include a Tech It Easy series on digital skills, with sessions scheduled at different libraries throughout November. The Gulf Breeze Library hosts a Senior Social on November 4 with coffee and games. The Navarre Library offers labARTory (an open art studio) on November 5 and Craft and Chat gatherings for needleworkers on November 6 and 20. All five libraries will hold a Veterans Appreciation Day on November 6 from 1–3 p.m. with refreshments. More details are available at www.santarosa.fl.gov/libraries.

item.title: Downtown Pensacola Lights Up Holiday Season Nov. 4 with Santa, Shopping, and Half-Million Lights
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Downtown Pensacola is kicking off the holiday season Wednesday, November 4th with a full slate of festive events centered on Palafox Street. Santa will arrive at 3:30 p.m. in front of the Pensacola Museum of History for photos and selfies until 4:45 p.m., when he'll flip the switch to illuminate more than half a million holiday lights stretching…
item.content:encoded:
Downtown Pensacola is kicking off the holiday season Wednesday, November 4th with a full slate of festive events centered on Palafox Street. Santa will arrive at 3:30 p.m. in front of the Pensacola Museum of History for photos and selfies until 4:45 p.m., when he'll flip the switch to illuminate more than half a million holiday lights stretching along Palafox and surrounding areas.

The evening's anchor event is the 10th Annual Holiday Haul, running from 5 p.m. to 8 p.m., featuring an open house atmosphere across downtown shops, galleries, and restaurants with live music, pop-ups, giveaways, and free trolley rides. The special Holiday Lights Edition of the Palafox Market will operate from 3:30 p.m. to 8 p.m. in Plaza Ferdinand, with local vendors selling homemade gifts, baked goods, and art. Visitors can also expect to see the Grinch and a mini-train circulating around Plaza Ferdinand throughout the evening.

The Downtown Improvement Board and local merchants are also launching the "All I Want" Holiday Giveaway, running through December 20th. Shoppers earn one raffle entry for every $10 spent at downtown businesses, with weekly prizes and a $1,000 grand prize in downtown gift cards. Double-entry opportunities occur on November 4th and Shop Small Saturday, November 28th. More details are available at www.downtownpensacola.com/AllIWant.

item.title: ECSO adds security to Ernest Ward Middle after TikTok threat investigation
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Escambia County Sheriff's Office is investigating a threat posted on TikTok targeting Ernest Ward Middle School in Walnut Hill, with extra deputies positioned on campus Tuesday as a precaution. According to the ECSO, investigators became aware of the social media post Monday and immediately launched an active inquiry into the matter. While…
item.content:encoded:
The Escambia County Sheriff's Office is investigating a threat posted on TikTok targeting Ernest Ward Middle School in Walnut Hill, with extra deputies positioned on campus Tuesday as a precaution.

According to the ECSO, investigators became aware of the social media post Monday and immediately launched an active inquiry into the matter. While details about the nature of the specific threat were not immediately disclosed, the agency determined the situation warranted heightened security presence at the school.

The deployment of additional law enforcement at the campus reflects standard protocol when schools face credible threats. Parents and guardians in the Ernest Ward attendance zone were likely notified of the increased security measures. The ECSO investigation is ongoing.
